Write site frequency spectra for dadi or fastsimcoal2

Source: R/write_sfs.R
write_sfs.Rd

Write site frequency spectra in the formats used by dadi (and moments) and by fastsimcoal2, as written by easySFS:

  • for an sfs object (as returned by pop_sfs(), pairwise_pop_sfs() and nwise_pop_sfs() with type = "array", or by the bootstrap_* functions, e.g. bootstrap_pop_sfs()), write that spectrum to file;

  • for a grouped gen_tibble, compute all the spectra that easySFS writes (the 1D spectrum of each population, the joint spectrum of each pair of populations, and the joint spectrum of all populations, in a single pass over the genotypes), and write them in out_dir, with the file names of easySFS, optionally with bootstrap replicates. Missing genotypes are dealt with by projecting each population down to n_proj allele copies (see pop_sfs()).

Usage

write_sfs(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfs'
write_sfs(
  x,
  file,
  format = c("dadi", "fastsimcoal2", "fastsimcoal2_multidimensional"),
  fastest = c("last", "first"),
  total_length = NULL,
  round = FALSE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'gen_tbl'
write_sfs(
  x,
  out_dir = NULL,
  format = c("dadi", "fastsimcoal2"),
  n_proj = NULL,
  prefix = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  total_length = NULL,
  round = FALSE,
  fastest = c("last", "first"),
  n_bootstrap = 0,
  bootstrap_block_size = NULL,
  bootstrap_size_unit = c("snp", "cM", "bp"),
  max_cells = 1e+07,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  block_size = bigstatsr::block_size(nrow(x), 1),
  ...
)

# Default S3 method
write_sfs(x, ...)

Arguments

x

an sfs object, or a grouped gen_tibble (as obtained by using dplyr::group_by()).

...

further arguments passed to the methods.

file

for an sfs object, the name of the file to write.

format

the format of the files: "dadi" or "fastsimcoal2"; for an sfs object, also "fastsimcoal2_multidimensional" (the multidimensional format of fastsimcoal2, whatever the number of populations). See details.

fastest

the order of the cells in dadi files and in the multidimensional fastsimcoal2 format: "last" (the default) keeps the order of the populations, so that the number of allele copies in the last population changes fastest, as in dadi and easySFS; "first" makes the number of copies in the first population change fastest. See details.

total_length

the total number of sites sequenced, including monomorphic ones, used to set the number of monomorphic sites (the first cell). If NULL (the default), the spectra are written as they are.

round

boolean, whether to round the number of sites in each cell to the nearest integer (as easySFS with --dtype int). Defaults to FALSE.

overwrite

boolean, whether to overwrite files that already exist. Defaults to FALSE.

out_dir

for a gen_tibble, the directory in which to write the files, or NULL (the default) to use the location and name of the backing files, followed by _dadi or _fastsimcoal2.

n_proj

the number of allele copies to project each population to: either a single value used for all populations, a vector with one value per population (in the order of the groups), or a vector named with the group labels. If NULL (the default), each population is projected to the number of allele copies that maximises its number of segregating sites (see pop_sfs_preview()).

prefix

for a gen_tibble written in fastsimcoal2 format, the prefix of the names of the 2D and multidimensional files, or NULL (the default) to use the name of the backing files.

folded

boolean, whether to fold the spectrum (the default, as the ancestral allele is not usually known). If FALSE, the spectrum is polarised with ancestral.

ancestral

the ancestral allele of each locus, used to polarise unfolded spectra: either the name of a column of the loci table (see show_loci()), or a character vector with one allele per locus (in the order of the loci table). Loci whose ancestral allele is missing (NA) or is neither of their alleles are dropped. If NULL (the default), the reference allele is taken to be ancestral, as in easySFS. Ignored, with a warning, for folded spectra.

n_bootstrap

for a gen_tibble, the number of bootstrap replicates to write (0, the default, for none).

bootstrap_block_size, bootstrap_size_unit

for a gen_tibble, the size of the blocks of loci resampled for the bootstrap, and its unit ("snp", the default, "cM" or "bp"); see bootstrap_pop_sfs().

max_cells

for a gen_tibble, the maximum number of cells of the joint spectrum of all populations; an error is raised for larger spectra.

n_cores

number of cores to be used, it defaults to bigstatsr::nb_cores()

block_size

maximum number of loci read at once.

Value

the path of the file (for an sfs object) or the paths of the files written (for a gen_tibble), invisibly.

Details

dadi format (format = "dadi"): a line with the dimensions of the spectrum (the number of allele copies of each population plus 1), folded or unfolded and the population labels in quotes; a line with the cells of the spectrum; and a line with the mask (1 for masked cells, see pop_sfs()). In dadi files, the cells are listed with the number of copies in the last population changing fastest. With fastest = "first", the populations are written in reverse order, so that the number of copies in the first population changes fastest and the file is still a valid dadi file.

fastsimcoal2 format (format = "fastsimcoal2"): for a 1D spectrum, as a _DAFpop0.obs (unfolded) or _MAFpop0.obs (folded) file; for a 2D spectrum, as a _jointDAFpop1_0.obs or _jointMAFpop1_0.obs file, a matrix with the second population in the rows (labelled d1_0, d1_1, ...) and the first population in the columns (labelled d0_0, d0_1, ...); for a spectrum of three or more populations, as a multidimensional spectrum (_MSFS.obs file). For an sfs object, format = "fastsimcoal2_multidimensional" writes the multidimensional format whatever the number of populations. In the multidimensional format, the cells are listed in the order set by fastest: "last" (the default) has the number of copies in the last population changing fastest, as written by easySFS; "first" has the first population changing fastest. Please check which order your version of fastsimcoal2 expects.

Monomorphic sites. As in easySFS, total_length gives the total number of sites sequenced (including monomorphic sites that are not in the gen_tibble): the first cell of the spectrum (sites with no copies of the alternate or minor allele) is then set to total_length minus the number of sites in all the other cells.

The spectra of a gen_tibble are written in out_dir, with the file names of easySFS (pop stands for the population labels, p for their projections, and M is replaced by D for unfolded spectra):

  • dadi: pop-p.sfs for each population, pop1-pop2.sfs for each pair, and pop1-pop2-...-popK.sfs for all populations;

  • fastsimcoal2: pop_MAFpop0.obs for each population, prefix_jointMAFpopj_i.obs for each pair (where i and j are the 0-based indices of the two populations, so that the second population of the pair is in the rows), and prefix_MSFS.obs for all populations.

easySFS writes these files in the sub-directories dadi and fastsimcoal2 of its output directory: use, for example, out_dir = file.path(dir, "dadi") with format = "dadi" and out_dir = file.path(dir, "fastsimcoal2") with format = "fastsimcoal2" to get the same layout. Populations are in the order of the groups (see dplyr::group_keys()): to change their order, which matters for dadi and fastsimcoal2 (and is set with --order in easySFS), change the order of the levels of the grouping variable (e.g. with factor()).

With n_bootstrap replicates of a block bootstrap (see bootstrap_pop_sfs()), the spectra of each replicate are also written, with the same file names, in the sub-directories bootstrap_1, bootstrap_2, ... of out_dir, numbered with as many digits as n_bootstrap (e.g. bootstrap_001 to bootstrap_100), which can be used to estimate confidence intervals with fastsimcoal2. Replicates use the same projections as the spectra of all loci, and total_length and round are applied to each of them. To draw the same replicates in both formats, set the same seed (with set.seed()) before writing each of them.

See also

pop_sfs(), pop_sfs_preview(), bootstrap_pop_sfs()

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

# write a single spectrum
sfs_2d <- example_gt %>%
  pairwise_pop_sfs(n_proj = 2, type = "array")
dadi_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".sfs")
write_sfs(sfs_2d$pop1.pop2, dadi_file)
readLines(dadi_file)
#> [1] "3 3 folded \"pop1\" \"pop2\""                                                                          
#> [2] "1.783333333333334 0.9333333333333336 0.3083333333333334 1.6 1.066666666666667 0 0.3083333333333334 0 0"
#> [3] "1 0 0 0 0 1 0 1 1"                                                                                     
fastsimcoal2_file <- tempfile(fileext = "_jointMAFpop1_0.obs")
write_sfs(sfs_2d$pop1.pop2, fastsimcoal2_file, format = "fastsimcoal2")
readLines(fastsimcoal2_file)
#> [1] "1 observation"                                 
#> [2] "\td0_0\td0_1\td0_2"                            
#> [3] "d1_0\t1.783333333333334 1.6 0.3083333333333334"
#> [4] "d1_1\t0.9333333333333336 1.066666666666667 0"  
#> [5] "d1_2\t0.3083333333333334 0 0"                  

# write all the spectra written by easySFS, in the same directories
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "example_sfs")
dadi_files <- example_gt %>%
  write_sfs(out_dir = file.path(out_dir, "dadi"), n_proj = 2)
basename(dadi_files)
#> [1] "pop1-2.sfs"         "pop2-2.sfs"         "pop3-2.sfs"        
#> [4] "pop1-pop2.sfs"      "pop1-pop3.sfs"      "pop2-pop3.sfs"     
#> [7] "pop1-pop2-pop3.sfs"
fastsimcoal2_files <- example_gt %>%
  write_sfs(
    out_dir = file.path(out_dir, "fastsimcoal2"), format = "fastsimcoal2",
    n_proj = 2, prefix = "example"
  )
basename(fastsimcoal2_files)
#> [1] "pop1_MAFpop0.obs"           "pop2_MAFpop0.obs"          
#> [3] "pop3_MAFpop0.obs"           "example_jointMAFpop1_0.obs"
#> [5] "example_jointMAFpop2_0.obs" "example_jointMAFpop2_1.obs"
#> [7] "example_MSFS.obs"          

# with 3 bootstrap replicates, resampling blocks of 2 SNPs
set.seed(1)
fastsimcoal2_files <- example_gt %>%
  write_sfs(
    out_dir = file.path(out_dir, "fastsimcoal2"), format = "fastsimcoal2",
    n_proj = 2, prefix = "example", n_bootstrap = 3,
    bootstrap_block_size = 2, overwrite = TRUE
  )
list.files(file.path(out_dir, "fastsimcoal2"))
#>  [1] "bootstrap_1"                "bootstrap_2"               
#>  [3] "bootstrap_3"                "example_MSFS.obs"          
#>  [5] "example_jointMAFpop1_0.obs" "example_jointMAFpop2_0.obs"
#>  [7] "example_jointMAFpop2_1.obs" "pop1_MAFpop0.obs"          
#>  [9] "pop2_MAFpop0.obs"           "pop3_MAFpop0.obs"
